Eli: Quick follow-up from todays All-hands pricing section. Couple of corner cases folks asked about during the q&a, collecting answers here. @Paula can you confirm?
Paula: Sure. Lay them out.
Eli: 1) Do unused monthly credits roll over if you upgrade mid-month? 2) If we change tiers mid-billing-cycle, is billing prorated?
Paula: Short answers: no for rollovers (unless explicitly part of a promo), yes for prorating on tier upgrades. We credit unused portion of the previous plan and charge the remainder for the new plan pro-rated to the billing day boundary. We show the math on the invoice.
Tom: Follow-up: what about switching from pay-as-you-go to a committed Dedicated contract mid-cycle? Any special handling?
Paula: For committed contracts we typically start the commitment on the contract start date. If you switch mid-month, we pro-rate the committed capacity fee and apply a one-time adjustment. Usage during the transition is billed against whichever model was active when the request ran.
Priya: Are trial/promo credits ever rolled into the first paid month automatically? One customer asked this during onboarding.
Paula: No automatic rollovers. Promo credits show an explicit expiry date in the Billing page. We can, however, grant discretionary credits for large customers during migration.
Eli: Another category: rate-limit headers and client retry guidance. Can we standardize headers returned by the API so client teams can implement smart backoffs?
Tom: We already return these headers on most endpoints: 
```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 17
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1713648000
X-Request-Id: req_abc123
```
Tom: We'll add a short doc fragment showing how to interpret Reset (unix epoch seconds) and Remaining.
Priya: What's the recommended retry strategy for 429s on burst drops? Exponential backoff + jitter? Any client libs we should reference?
Tom: Yes, exponential backoff with capped max delay + jitter. For streaming/generation clients we also recommend checkpointing the prompt state so retries don't cause duplicate charges. We'll add a sample in the Node and Python SDKs.
BillingBot: Billing notice: sample invoice template uploaded to Billing > Examples. Link: https://internal.redwood/billing/invoice-samples
Eli: One more: admin keys vs service keys. If a team accidentally leaks an admin key, do we auto-revoke and rotate? What's the blast-radius reduction guidance?
Paula: We strongly advise using short-lived service keys for apps and reserve admin keys for console actions. If a key is leaked, rotate immediately; we can revoke keys at the org level. For enterprise customers we offer KMS-backed key controls and access logs. We'll publish a quick-runbook for rotating keys and steps to audit recent requests (hint: X-Request-Id + request logs).
Priya: Can we add UI warnings in Console Billing when a promo credit is expiring within 7 days? That would help onboardings.
Paula: Good suggestion. I'll add to the Billing roadmap item: "Show expiring credits and suggested plans" and aim for a small UI banner in the next sprint.
Eli: Action items: @Paula to add invoice worked examples + promo expiry banner ticket, @Tom to add header docs + retry snippets to SDK readmes, @Priya to draft a key-rotation runbook we can link from the Console. I'll ping this thread when the docs are live. Thanks all :thumbsup:
